subject: ss-gastroenterology
title: Helicobacter Pylori and Peptic Ulcer Disease

steps.tx: The **Maastricht VI** Florence consensus report provides updated guidelines for managing Helicobacter pylori infection. In regions with clarithromycin resistance exceeding **15%**, standard triple therapy is contraindicated. First-line empiric treatment requires a **14**-day course of **bismuth quadruple therapy** comprising a proton pump inhibitor, bismuth subcitrate or subsalicylate, tetracycline, and metronidazole. Alternatively, potassium-competitive acid blocker vonoprazan-based regimens provide superior acid suppression and eradication rates without requiring bismuth.

steps.tx: The **urea breath test**, using carbon-**13** or carbon-**14**, shows live bacterial urease. The monoclonal **stool antigen test** shows antigen the organism is shedding, not urease. Neither result means old exposure. Stop a proton pump inhibitor for at least **14** days, and stop antibiotics or bismuth for at least **28** days, or a suppressed bacterial load makes either test falsely negative.

steps.tx: The **Correa cascade** demonstrates the sequential histological progression from normal gastric mucosa to invasive intestinal-type gastric adenocarcinoma. Chronic infection triggers superficial active gastritis, progressing over decades to multifocal chronic atrophic gastritis with glandular loss. Subsequent replacement of specialized gastric epithelium by Goblet cells creates **intestinal metaplasia**, which evolves into low-grade and high-grade dysplasia. Eradicating Helicobacter pylori before extensive intestinal metaplasia greatly cuts later cancer risk, but that risk does not fall to zero.

steps.tx: While duodenal ulcers are almost universally benign and do not require routine repeat endoscopic visualization, **gastric ulcers** carry a significant risk of harboring underlying adenocarcinoma. Following initial diagnosis and biopsy of a gastric ulcer, clinicians must prescribe medical acid suppression for **6** to **8** weeks. A mandatory **surveillance endoscopy** with repeat quadrant biopsies must follow to document complete mucosal healing and rigorously exclude ulcerated malignancy masquerading as benign disease.

left.title: Duodenal Peptic Ulcers
points: Follow-up: No surveillance endoscopy needed if asymptomatic
Pathology: Acid hypersecretion driven by antral gastritis

right.title: Gastric Peptic Ulcers
points: Malignancy risk: Up to 5% harbor adenocarcinoma
Follow-up: Mandatory endoscopy at 6 to 8 weeks
Pathology: Mucosal barrier breakdown from pangastritis

steps.tx: **NSAID-induced ulcers** develop through dual mechanisms combining direct chemical irritation and systemic biochemical suppression. Systemic absorption of non-selective nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs inhibits mucosal **cyclooxygenase-1**, preventing conversion of arachidonic acid into cytoprotective PGE2 and PGI2. This prostaglandin depletion diminishes gastric mucosal blood flow, decreases mucus and bicarbonate production, and impairs cellular restitution, predisposing to silent mucosal ulceration and life-threatening haemorrhage.

steps.tx: **Zollinger-Ellison syndrome** is characterized by severe refractory peptic ulceration and secretory diarrhoea resulting from an autonomous gastrinoma. Diagnosis is established by demonstrating a fasting serum gastrin exceeding **1000** pg/mL in the setting of gastric hyperacidity with a pH below **2**. In borderline cases where serum gastrin is mildly elevated, a **secretin stimulation test** is diagnostic: intravenous injection of secretin produces a paradoxical elevation in serum gastrin exceeding **120** pg/mL above baseline.

steps.tx: Gastric **MALT lymphoma** represents an extranodal marginal zone B-cell neoplasm arising in response to chronic Helicobacter pylori antigen stimulation. Up to **75%** to **80%** of patients with stage **1** localized gastric MALT lymphoma achieve complete and durable disease remission following successful **bacterial eradication** alone. Lesions bearing the t(11;18)(q21;q21) BIRC3-MALT1 chromosomal translocation, however, exhibit constitutive NF-kappaB activation and are notoriously unresponsive to antibiotic therapy, requiring systemic therapy or involved-site radiation.

left.title: t(11;18) Negative MALT Lymphoma
points: Responds to H. pylori eradication in 75% to 80%

right.title: t(11;18) Translocation Positive

steps.tx: The clinical virulence of Helicobacter pylori is largely dictated by major strain-specific pathogenicity factors. The **CagA** cytotoxin-associated gene A is delivered into host gastric epithelial cells via a bacterial type IV secretion system, where it undergoes tyrosine phosphorylation by Src family kinases and disrupts intracellular signaling. Along with the pore-forming **VacA** vacuolating cytotoxin A, strains harboring CagA induce potent interleukin-8 production, severe pangastritis, and dramatically heightened rates of peptic ulceration and gastric adenocarcinoma.
